messages.author: ba3b508d5a663f81
messages.subject: Exporting data from rqtl
parts:
Hello,

I am using the Rstudio and see how I can export plots. I am trying to figure out how to export things like the results from scanone or scantwo, or the genetic map data to an excel file, meaning the markers and centimorgan position for each one. Can anyone help?

Thank you!

-Ben

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Exporting data from rqtl
parts:
The main way that I export graphs is to use one of the graphics device functions, principally pdf() or png().

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)

pdf("hyper_scanone.pdf", height=7.5, width=10, pointsize=14)
plot(out, bgrect="gray92", bandcol="gray82")
dev.off()

I think there's also an "export" button on the plot pane in RStudio.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Exporting data from rqtl
parts:
Ah, sorry; I guess I should read all of the words in your post.

To save a map to a file, you first need to convert it from a list to something rectangular. You can use the function map2table().

mymap_table <- map2table(mymap)
write.csv(mymap_table, "mymap.csv")

scanone output is already a table, so write.csv() should work. scantwo output are a bit of a mess; I can't think of an easy way to save them to an excel file.

cross data can be saved to a file with write.cross().

karl
